extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria from the MPEP (37 CFR 1.703–1.705 and 1.704(f)) governing when and how patent term adjustment (PTA) is calculated, what periods count or are excluded, and procedural requirements for avoiding or seeking reinstatement of PTA. Includes definitions (e.g., "in condition for examination"), safe-harbors for IDS submissions, and filing/fee/deadline requirements for PTA reconsideration or reinstatement requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for examination (37 CFR 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when the application includes a specification, including at least one claim and an abstract (§ 1.72(b)), and has papers in compliance with § 1.52, drawings (if any) in compliance with § 1.84, any English translation required by § 1.52(d) or § 1.57(a), a sequence listing in compliance with § 1.821 through § 1.825 (if applicable), the inventor’s oath or declaration or an application data sheet containing the information specified in § 1.63(b), the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(a) or § 1.16(c)), the search fee (§ 1.16(k) or § 1.16(m)), the examination fee (§ 1.16(o) or § 1.16(q)), any certified copy of the previously filed application required by § 1.57(a), and any application size fee required by the Office under § 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications entering the national stage, analogous national-stage documents and fees (including search and examination fees per § 1.492) are required. Papers/drawings/sequence listings corrected prior to the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 are considered in compliance for purposes of this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS 30-day safe harbor (37 CFR 1.704(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98, or an RCE under § 1.114 containing only such an IDS, will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution if the paper or RCE is accompanied by a statement that each item of information in the IDS: (i) was first cited in any communication from a patent office in a counterpart foreign or international application or from the Office and that communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to the filing of the IDS; or (ii) is a communication issued by a patent office in a counterpart foreign or international application or by the Office and this communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to the filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thirty-day period is not extendable. Effective Dec. 1, 2011 and subsequent amendments expanded the safe harbor to Office communications as well as foreign-office communications. Effective March 10, 2015, a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 with only an IDS will not be considered a failure if accompanied by the required statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-only submission not a failure when accompanying statement provided
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an IDS in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under certain paragraphs of § 1.704 if accompanied by the required statement about the origin and timing of the cited items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule applies to avoid PTA reduction in cases where the IDS results from communications from a foreign or the Office, provided the timing requirements and the required statement are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirty-day IDS timing is non-extendable
rubrics_metrics.description: The thirty-day period set forth in paragraph (d)(1) of § 1.704 is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file the IDS and required statement within 30 days of receipt by a designated individual (§ 1.56(c)); no extensions are available for this safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of reinstatement under § 1.705(c) not a failure (37 CFR 1.704(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application under paragraph (c)(10) of § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a timely reinstatement request itself will not trigger a PTA-reduction failure finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing application prosecution — pre-filing period excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Further prosecution via a continuing application is a circumstance in which the period of adjustment set forth in § 1.703 shall not include any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments over time have renumbered the relevant paragraphs, but the substance is that delay attributable to activity in an earlier-filed application (prior to the filing date of the patent-bearing application) is not counted toward PTA for the later patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions that qualify as 'action under 35 U.S.C. 132' (counts toward PTA stop-the-clock)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written restriction requirement, a written election of species requirement, a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, an action under Ex parte Quayle, and a notice of allowability (PTOL-37) are each an action issued as a result of the examination conducted pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 131 and are notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office notices and letters issued as part of pre-examination processing (e.g., Notice of Incomplete Nonprovisional Application, Notice of Omitted Item(s), Notice to File Missing Parts, Notice of Informal Application, Notice to File Corrected Application Papers Filing Date Granted, Notice to Comply with Requirements for Sequence Disclosures) are not notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132 and therefore do not count as examiner actions for purposes of measuring PTA under the 14-month/other timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a) — general rule (sum of (a)(1)–(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under § 1.702(a) is the sum of the periods specified in 37 CFR 1.703(a)(1) through 1.703(a)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subparagraphs enumerate distinct start and end dates for portions of the adjustment (e.g., 14 months after filing until Office action or notice of allowance, 4-month rules after certain applicant filings, etc.). Overlaps between these periods must be handled per paragraph (f) (overlap rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(1) — 14-month examination delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is fourteen months after the date on which the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (or the date the national stage commenced under 35 U.S.C. 371(b) or (f) for international applications) and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132, or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications, the fourteen-month measurement date may be the date of commencement of the national stage; AIA Technical Corrections changed the start-date mechanics for some international cases. Office actions issued as part of examination (including certain notices like restriction requirements) count; pre-examination notices do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(2) — 4-month period after reply under § 1.111
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 was filed and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts days if the Office does not act within four months after certain applicant replies under § 1.111; the start is four months after the applicant filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(3) — 4-month period after reply in compliance with § 1.113(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date a reply in compliance with § 1.113(c) was filed and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply in compliance with § 1.113 is a reply to a final Office action that cancels all rejected claims and removes all outstanding objections and requirements or otherwise places the application in condition for allowance. After-final amendments that do not accomplish those things do not trigger the 1.703(a)(3) four-month counting requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(4) — 4-month period after filing of an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 was filed and ending on the date of mailing of any of an examiner’s answer under § 41.39, an action under 35 U.S.C. 132, or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37’ requires compliance with the form/content rules in § 41.37(c) and, historically, payment of the appeal brief fee; for appeal briefs filed on or after March 19, 2013 the fee associated with the appeal brief was set to zero dollars, so fee payment is not required for those filings. The statutory phrase 'the date on which an appeal was taken' is interpreted as the date the appeal brief was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(5) — 4-month period after final decision by Board or court
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date of a final decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or by a Federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 where at least one allowable claim remains in the application and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Allowable claims remain in the application’ means at least one pending claim that is not withdrawn and is not subject to a rejection/objection; the MPEP gives specific examples (A-C) illustrating when claims count. A Board decision is a qualifying 'decision' only if it sustains or reverses rejections or, in limited circumstances, a remand may be deemed a decision (see remand guidance). A Board decision containing a new ground of rejection under § 41.50(b) is not a 'final decision' for purposes of 1.703(a)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(6) — 4-month period after issue fee payment and satisfaction of requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date the issue fee was paid and all outstanding requirements were satisfied and ending on the date a patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine the period under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)(iv), look back from the issue date to the most recent date on which the issue fee or another requirement was outstanding; the four-month clock then runs from that date forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b) — 3-year rule and excluded periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under § 1.702(b) is the number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is three years after the date on which the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (or the national stage commenced) and ending on the date a patent was issued, but not including specified excluded periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The excluded periods include: (1) days during which a request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) was pending until mailing of the notice of allowance; (2) days during instituted interference or derivation proceedings and suspensions due to such proceedings; (3) secrecy/sealed condition periods and related exceptions (with subparts (i)-(iv)); and (4) periods during which jurisdiction is with the PTAB under § 41.35(a) until jurisdiction ends. Each excluded period is detailed in the regulation and MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(c)/(d)/(e) — interference/secrecy/PTAB-jurisdiction adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs (c) through (e) specify additional categories of PTA under §§ 1.702(c)–(e): (c) sums periods for interference/derivation institution and suspension due to other interferences; (d) sums periods the application was maintained under secrecy (35 U.S.C. 181) and related secrecy notification windows; (e) sums days from PTAB jurisdiction transfer to the date of final decision in favor of applicant by the PTAB or a Federal court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These paragraphs are limited to non-overlapping periods and must be measured precisely from the institution/termination or transfer/final-decision dates. For (e), the final decision must be in favor of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules, overlap, and maximum adjustment (37 CFR 1.703(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period is indicated as 'beginning' on a particular day, that day is included in the period (i.e., 'day one'). The end of the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.703(a) and (b) is 'day zero' as to the period of adjustment, whereas the first day of the proceedings set forth in 1.703(c)-(e) is 'day one'. To the extent that periods attributable to the specified grounds overlap, the period of adjustment shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed. The term shall be adjusted for the sum of the periods calculated under paragraphs (a) through (e), to the extent not overlapping, less the sum of the periods calculated under § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a period beginning April 1 and ending April 10 counts as ten days. Overlaps must be removed so total PTA does not exceed real issuance delay; subtract periods attributable to applicant delay per § 1.704.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of 'allowable claims remain in the application' (for 1.703(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)(iii), 'allowable claims remain in the application' means that after the decision there is at least one pending claim that is not withdrawn and is not subject to a rejection, objection, or other requirement. Examples: (A) if claim 2 was indicated as allowable prior to appeal and claim 1's rejection is affirmed, then allowable claims remain; (B) if claim 2 is objected to as allowable except for dependency on claim 1, then allowable claims do not remain; (C) if claim 2's rejection is reversed on appeal and is not subject to any outstanding objection, then allowable claims remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP provides concrete claim configurations to illustrate when the PTAB/court decision triggers the 1.703(a)(5) timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'final decision' for purposes of 1.703(a)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'final decision' means: (1) the decision is the last decision in the review by the Board (or by a federal court); and (2) the decision does not require further action by the applicant to avoid termination of proceedings as to the rejected claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board decision containing a new ground of rejection under § 41.50(b) requires action by the applicant and therefore is not a 'final decision' for 1.703(a)(5). A Board decision reversing all rejections on appeal can be 'final' for 1.703(a)(5) even if judicial review remains possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand as a 'decision' in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is remanded by a panel and the remand is the last action by a panel of the Board prior to the mailing of a notice of allowance, the remand generally shall be considered a decision by the Board for purposes of 37 CFR 1.703(a)(5) (and related provisions), and may be considered a final decision in favor of the applicant in certain contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remand is not considered a 'decision reversing an adverse determination' if, after the remand, a request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) was filed that was not first preceded by the mailing, after the remand, of at least one action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.705(b) — PTA reconsideration application requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the patent term adjustment indicated on the patent must be by way of an application for patent term adjustment filed no later than two months from the date the patent was granted (this two-month period may be extended under § 1.136(a)). The application must be accompanied by: (1) the fee set forth in § 1.18(e); and (2) a statement of the facts specifying the correct PTA and the basis or bases under § 1.702, the relevant dates as specified in §§ 1.703(a)–(e) and the adjustment as specified in § 1.703(f), whether the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer and its expiration, and (iv) either circumstances during prosecution constituting a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under § 1.704 or that there were no such circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for reconsideration must itemize the factual bases and dates underlying the claimed PTA; failure to provide required information or fee may be fatal. The two-month window is extendable under general extension rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.705(c) — Reinstatement of PTA reduction for failure to reply within three months
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement of all or part of the period of adjustment reduced pursuant to § 1.704(b) for failing to reply to a rejection, objection, argument, or other request within three months of the date of mailing of the Office communication must be filed prior to issuance of the patent. This time period is not extendable. The request must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.18(f) and a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that, in spite of all due care, the applicant was unable to reply within three months. The Office shall not grant any request for reinstatement for more than three additional months for each reply beyond three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the 'due care' showing for PTA reinstatement; must be filed before patent issues and requires a factual showing that the delay was despite all due care, with limits on amount of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions on PTA not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: No submission or petition on behalf of a third party concerning patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) will be considered by the Office; any such submission or petition will be returned to the third party or otherwise disposed of at the convenience of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA adjudications and reconsideration requests are strictly parties' matters; third-party petitions are not a vehicle for altering PTA determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day-counting example and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period is indicated as 'beginning' on a particular day, that day is included in the period (i.e., 'day one'). For example, a period beginning on April 1 and ending on April 10 is ten (not nine) days in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inclusive counting principle applies to the start date of periods specified in 37 CFR 1.703; other provisions distinguish 'day zero' and 'day one' depending on context (see 1.703(f)).
